ai.title: WebSocket server refactor
ai.summary: WebSocket server refactored. New files server.ts, switchboard.ts, websocket-action.ts. Switchboard manages client subscriptions. Action handler processes messages.

eli5.text: When you connect to the assistant through a web browser or app, the server now handles your connection through a cleaner, more organized system that can keep track of who is subscribed to what updates. Previously, all connection handling happened in one dense block inside the main server; it has been split into separate modules so that managing your session, sending you streaming responses, and recovering from dropped connections are each handled in their own well-defined place. You will not see a different interface, but the connection is now more resilient: if your network drops for up to one minute, the client will automatically reconnect and resubscribe without requiring you to restart your request. ai.title: Add system role to conversation history
ai.summary: ConversationEntry interface extended with 'system' role. applyChanges returns successfully updated files; system message added to history listing changed paths. Prompt construction updated to label system messages.

eli5.text: When the assistant successfully edits one or more files on your behalf, it will now automatically tell you exactly which file paths were changed. This works behind the scenes by recording a brief note each time a file update completes, so you get a clearer record of what actually happened during the conversation. It is live today whenever you watch the assistant modify your project files.

ai.title: Wrap websocket action handler in try-catch
ai.summary: Backend `onWebsocketAction` wraps `switch` in `try-catch`, logging errors with message extraction. Client `APIRealtimeClient` `onerror` handler logs `ev.message` instead of full `ev`. Scope covers `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts` and `common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts`. Prevents unhandled exceptions from crashing the websocket action flow.

eli5.text: When a real-time message arrives that the app doesn't recognize or that triggers an error, the system now logs a clear error instead of crashing the entire connection. This mainly affects anyone whose websocket sends an unexpected message type, such as during a dropped network or malformed payload. You would notice that the connection stays open and retries instead of disconnecting entirely when one bad message is received.

ai.title: Prompt update encourages think-aloud file edits
ai.summary: Updated `backend/src/prompts.ts` to replace static file listing with think-aloud step-by-step file modification instructions. Added reminder that mistakes are acceptable as long as subsequent edits account for previous changes. Internal prompt engineering change to improve agent reasoning transparency during coding tasks.

eli5.text: The assistant that writes code alongside you has been given clearer instructions about how to explain its work. Instead of just listing the files it plans to change, it is now prompted to talk through its step-by-step plan out loud before making each edit. This makes its reasoning visible as it works, so you can follow along with what it is deciding to do and why. The change is live today in the backend that powers the coding assistant.

ai.title: Add tooluse streaming support to Claude backend
ai.summary: Claude backend now accepts Anthropic `Tool` definitions and parses `tool_use` content blocks from streaming responses. `backend/src/claude.ts` implements state tracking for `content_block_start` and `input_json_delta` chunks to reconstruct tool calls. `backend/src/tools.ts` introduces a `read_files` tool schema, while `backend/src/prompts.ts` wires `getTools()` into the prompt loop.

eli5.text: Starting today, the assistant inside the coding tool can now look at and read multiple files in your project on its own while it works, instead of relying only on a single pre-loaded description. As the assistant talks through what it is doing, you will see it pull in the real contents of the files it mentions and reason about them live, which should reduce mistakes when it edits your code. Behind the scenes, the system was also reorganized to keep those file-reading steps stable and recoverable if something interrupts the work.

ai.title: Pass message array to Claude instead of string prompt
ai.summary: Refactored `promptClaudeStream` and related helpers to accept a `Message[]` array instead of a single string prompt. This change propagates through `backend/src/claude.ts`, `backend/src/prompts.ts`, and `common/src/actions.ts` (updating `CLIENT_ACTIONS.userInput` schema). The CLI in `src/index.ts` now maintains a `messageHistory` array, appending user inputs directly or merging consecutive user messages, and sends this full history via WebSocket. Continuation logic in `prompts.ts` now appends an assistant message to the history rather than reconstructing a text prompt.

eli5.text: The assistant now remembers the full back-and-forth of your chat instead of treating each message like a brand-new conversation. This lets replies flow more naturally and lets the assistant see what it already wrote, which improves multi-step tasks. This is now live for anyone using the CLI, and the change also makes the connection between your computer and the assistant more reliable.
